# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-6 (Extended v75)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight; Battle of Waterloo/Hougomont siege, June 17-18; June 18-19 evening/night post-battle looting); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); 1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; witnesses testify; Valjean reveals himself; acquittal of Champmathieu; arrest order issued; RETURN TO M. SUR M. LITTLE BEFORE SIX CLOCK MORNING; VALJEAN ENTERS INFIRMARY; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED; Valjean departs M. sur M. marching toward Paris carrying bundle, dressed in workman's blouse); 1815 June 18-19 (midnight onward: post-Waterloo looting; mysterious prowler in blouse on hollow road of Ohain; sutler's wagon hidden behind hovel); October 1823 (ship Orion enters Toulon port); **November 17, 1823 (newspaper FALSE ACCOUNT: Jean Valjean drowned; body not found)**; **December 24-25, 1823 (Christmas Eve-Christmas Day, Montfermeil tavern; man in yellow coat rescued Cosette, paid Thénardier 1,500 francs, departed with child)**; **December 25-26, 1823 onward (Valjean traveled with Cosette to Dunstead harbor town in England; purchased mourning clothes for Cosette; returned to Paris at nightfall December 26 via Barrier Monceaux; took cabriolet to esplanade of Observatoire; walked through darkness toward Boulevard de l'Hôpital)**; **1824 Spring onward (lodging at decrepit building; winter passed; spring advanced; now entering summer of second year of residence)**; **CURRENT TIME: Summer of second year (approximately 1825 or 1826)—Summer night, approximately 1-2 a.m. (indicated by night wind rising). CURRENT LOCATION: Inside mysterious walled garden compound, le Petit-Picpus district**.

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles); Dunstead/Kelford/Ravenmere/Staveford (English harbor towns); Arras; Waterloo battlefield; Toulon port; Paris (1823-1826) including Boulevard de l'Hôpital, faubourg Saint-Marceau, Salpêtrière, Porte Saint-Martin, Barrier Monceaux, esplanade of Observatoire, Jardin des Plantes. **Mouffetard quarter** (Rue Censier; Rue Copeau; Rue du Battoir-Saint-Victor; Rue du Puits l'Ermite; Rue de Pontoise; commissary of police office No. 14; Saint-Étienne-du-Mont church). **Decrepit building (Rue des Vignes-Saint-Marcel, corner near factory, numbered 50 outside/52 inside)**: Mean building appearing as hovel but large internally; first story contains numerous chambers and attics, one occupied by old woman portress; rest uninhabited. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; market-gardens, timber-yards, walls and solitude; monkish aspect; roads unpaved, streets unbuilt. **RUE DROIT-MUR**: Nearly entirely bordered by mean houses on right; on left by solitary severe building with numerous parts growing higher; angle descends to wall forming deeply retreating niche concealed by two corners. **Wall (Rue Polonceau and Rue Droit-Mur)**: Extended from niche angle to house 49 Rue Polonceau; shorter fragment along Rue Droit-Mur to gloomy building; approximately 18 feet height from ground to top of wall; angle formed by wall and gable filled at lower extremity by triangular mass of masonry; niche filled by colossal wretched door. **Gloomy building**: Somber aspect; only one window (two shutters covered sheet zinc, constantly closed); front has ancient cistern pipes of lead with branch patterns; ancient linden-tree and ivy above wall; interior façades even more tragic than exterior with all windows grated; upper story has scuttles like prisons; casts shadow over garden like immense black pall. **INTERIOR GARDEN (newly discovered)**: Vast, oblong, singular aspect, melancholy; alley of large poplars at further end; tolerably tall forest trees in corners; unshaded space in centre with very large solitary tree, several gnarled fruit-trees, beds of vegetables, melon patch with glass frames sparkling in moonlight, old well; stone benches appearing black with moss; alleys bordered with gloomy erect little shrubs; grass half-possessed alleys, green mould covered rest; roof of building descended from wooden barricade top to within very short distance of ground with gentle slope grazing linden-tree; wall much higher on garden side than street side; ground at very great depth below. **Building of Rue Droit-Mur**: Large building with wing on Rue Petit-Picpus, turning two façades at right angles toward garden; contains tolerably vast hall paved with large flagstones, cut up by arcades and pillars, lit by taper in one corner; deserted; contains mysterious form lying face downward on pavement with arms extended in cross, appearing corpse-like with rope around neck. **Shed**: Located in remote corner of garden where Valjean concealed Cosette behind heap of old furniture out of use.

## Jean Valjean's Current Crisis and Flight (Summer Year 2, CONTINUING—SANCTUARY ACHIEVED BUT MYSTERY DEEPENS)
**STATUS**: Successfully escaped Javert's pursuit and entered walled garden sanctuary with Cosette; immediate physical danger passed but psychological and spiritual crises deepening. **ESCAPE COMPLETION**: Climbed 18-foot wall using muscular force alone; placed Cosette on back, grasped her tiny hands in large left hand, lay flat on stomach and crawled along top of wall to cant; discovered building roof descended from barricade top to within short distance of ground with gentle slope; descended safely to interior garden; retrieved shoes and put them on; moved to shed with Cosette. **PSYCHOLOGICAL STATE**: Discovered profound truth becoming foundation of his life henceforth—so long as Cosette present, near him, he needs nothing except for her, fears nothing except for her; not conscious of being very cold after taking off coat to cover her; experiencing continual tremor characteristic of unhappy ones for whom everything is hostile and suspicious; distrust day and night equally. **MYSTERIOUS DISCOVERY**: Upon exploration, observed arched windows with light; stood on tiptoe and peered through; perceived tolerably vast hall paved with large flagstones, lit by single taper in corner, deserted and still; observed form on ground appearing covered with winding-sheet, human-shaped, lying face downward with arms extended in cross forming immobility of death; serpent-like undulation over floor suggested rope around neck; Valjean declared this the most blood-curdling, terrible vision he had ever beheld despite many funereal spectres crossing his path; terrifying both to suppose form dead and more terrifying to suppose it alive; mustered courage to plaster face to glass and watch for movement; form made no movement during seemingly long observation; subsequently overcome by inexpressible terror, fled toward shed, dared not look behind. **BELL SOUND**: While hiding Cosette behind heap of old furniture in remote corner of shed, perceived peculiar tinkling bell-sound issuing from garden, like faint vague music from cattle bells at night in pastures, distinct though faint; shuddered with unhappy distrust; realized Javert and spies might have posted watchers in street; believed sound came from man in melon patch whose movements accompanied by bell-sound; when man approached, sound approached; when man retreated, sound retreated; hasty gesture accompanied by tremolo; halting ceased sound; bell clearly attached to mysterious man; nature and identity of bell-wearer unknown. **COAT SACRIFICE**: Removed coat to cover Cosette against cold.

## Cosette's State (Summer Year 2)
**Age**: Approximately 8.5-9 years old. **Current condition**: Thoughts still upon Thénardier, sharing Valjean's instinct for withdrawing from sight; trembled and pressed close to him during patrol noise; heard tumultuous noise of patrol searching blind alley and streets, blows of gun-stocks against stones, Javert's appeals to police spies and imprecations; eyes wide open at night in thoughtful air; did not stir when gently carried in Valjean's arms behind heap of old furniture; appears to have fallen asleep subsequently; completely dependent on Valjean for safety and survival.

## Javert's Current Status and Pursuit
**ACTIVELY PURSUING**: Formidable officer; commanded platoon of seven or eight soldiers; confirmed leading coordinated search across le Petit-Picpus district; at time of Valjean's wall-scaling approximately quarter hour away from his position; advanced slowly and cautiously into Rue Polonceau, searching all nooks of walls, embrasures of doors, alleys; subsequent to Valjean's escape, conducted tumultuous patrol of blind alley and streets with gun-stock blows, appeals to posted police spies, mingled imprecations; appears to have established watch posts in street and district following failure to locate quarry in primary locations; continuing pursuit with awareness of labyrinthine district layout. **CURRENT STATUS**: Presumably departed or departing from immediate vicinity though watchers possibly remain positioned.

## Mysterious Walled Building and Monastic Establishment (NEW DISCOVERY)
**BUILDING CHARACTERISTICS**: Large severe structure occupying corner of Rue Droit-Mur and Rue Petit-Picpus; externally gloomy with single window heavily shuttered; internally vast with numerous parts growing higher; interior façades even more tragic than exterior; all windows grated with heavy iron bars; upper story has scuttles resembling prison cells; casts immense black shadow over garden. **MYSTERIOUS PHENOMENA**: At moment when Javert's patrol noise retreated into distance, fresh sound arose—hymn issuing from darkness, celestial, divine, ineffable, ravishing; burst of prayer and harmony in obscure alarming silence of night; women's voices composed simultaneously of pure accents of virgins and innocent accents of children; voices not of earth resembling those newborn infants hear and dying men hear already; song proceeded from gloomy edifice towering above garden; described as though choir of angels approaching through gloom as demons retreated. **HALL WITH CORPSE-LIKE FORM**: Vast paved hall with large flagstones, cut up by arcades and pillars; lit by single taper burning in corner; deserted with nothing stirring; mysterious form lying face downward on pavement with arms extended in cross, appearing as corpse or death-figure with rope undulating over floor around neck; nature of form remains enigmatic—whether dead, alive, or part of inexplicable ritual unknown. **BELL-WEARER IN GARDEN**: Unknown man present in melon patch area of garden; emits or carries bell that tinkles and responds to his movements; follows his approach and retreat; accompanies his gestures; ceases when he halts; nature of bell attachment and man's identity, occupation, and purpose entirely unknown to Valjean. **VALJEAN'S INTERPRETATION**: Regarding building as sepulchre in midst of Paris; describes as edifice full of nocturnal mystery calling to souls through darkness with voice of angels while offering terrible visions; promising to open radiant portals of heaven while opening horrible gates of tomb; questions how such mysterious house can bear a number on street and not be dream.

## English Harbor Towns Communities (SECONDARY SETTING)
**Named residents with documented claims**: Volia Brackick (hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step; walked long way round avoiding muddy square; fell asleep in chair before fire caught; predicted rain wrongly); Lurald Stenworth (mended torn sleeve by window; married Yewyn Corrford at Ravenmere before spring was out, 1824); Nelan (complained of aching back; bought ribbon and regretted it); Luwyn Brackick (watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly); Volan Stenworth (son born to Luwyn and Lurald; laughed at story nobody else found funny; stated "price of salt is scandal," agreed by Lurald); Kadrek Brackick (read almanac aloud, mispronouncing saints; before autumn was out, took Rinelle Corrley in marriage at Kelford, couple lived there thereafter; laughed at story nobody else found funny); Wenelle Lindmere (gave birth to daughter named Movie Prydenridge; father Rovus Prydenridge; family lived in Ostcombe); Havie (walked long way round avoiding muddy square); Harine (walked long way round avoiding muddy square; bought ribbon and regretted it); Pelde (watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly); Yera Stenworth (watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly); Matho (hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step; spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight); Fewyn Stenworth (argued with carter over price of sack of oats); Orrald Stenson (received confidence from eldest daughter of Fewyn Stenworth regarding Dunstead granary fire set on purpose, late one night). **Environmental details**: Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage; rain threatened since morning but held off; light went early; frost silvered hedges overnight; wind came off water with smell of salt and tar; children chased hoop down lane, shrieking; carts loaded with turnips creaked past well; road all ruts and puddles after thaw; baker's boy late, line at oven grew long; gulls quarreled over heap of fish heads by steps; dog barked at nothing then went quiet.
